thread.title: Morning Report APAC: Asian markets rise on US jobs strength

author: Althea Spinozzi
title: Morning Report APAC: Asian markets rise on US jobs strength
text: United States Dow (+440 points) and S&P 500 (+47 points) closed off higher after February jobs growth far exceeded expectations. The US economy added 313,000 jobs in February, well above estimates of 200,000, according to FactSet. The unemployment rate held at a 17-year low of 4.1%. Shares of Goldman Sachs Group Inc (GS) shares were up 1.66%, and last traded at 270.77 on a report from The Wall Street Journal that said CEO Lloyd Blankfein was preparing to step down from the firm as soon as the end of the year. Netflix Inc (NFLX) shares rose 4.56% to 331.44, and hit a 52-week high on Friday following a report that former President Barack Obama was in "advanced" talks to produce a series of exclusive programs for the video streaming company. Following this, a report says Apple (AAPL) and Amazon.com (AMZN) have also expressed interest in talking with the Obamas about content deals on their own streaming services. Wynn Resorts (WYNN) rolled ahead 5.46% and closed at 188.89, after reports that the company had agreed to pay $2.6 billion to settle a shareholder dispute. The payment aims to allow Steve Wynn, who resigned as chairman and chief executive in February amid allegations of sexual misconduct, to sell his 12% stake in the company. The stock ended Thursday up 9.8% for the week after a five-day advance. The gain lifted shares back above 10-week support. Europe The main European stock markets finished on a positive note, following a better-than-expected jobs report from out of the US. UK's FTSE gained 21 points and Germany's Dax closed off slightly lower -8 points. In individual stocks news, British satellite firm Inmarsat (ISAT) saw shares slipped 6.7% to £432.70 after it reported earnings and said that it had cut its dividend, in order to spend more on delivering wi-fi on commercial planes, according to Reuters. Gaming company GVC Holdings PLC (GVC) posted a full-year net gaming revenue rise of 17% in 2017. The online gambling firm said its latest figures were lifted by gains from the Bwin.party business it bought three years ago. Shares of GVC Holdings jumped 5% to £945.50. Hong Kong Hang Seng Index (HSI) jumped 341points / 1.11% to 30,996 points. Hong Kong stocks followed US market higher, approaching 31,000, as Donald Trump slapped import duties on steel and aluminium but temporarily exempted Canada and Mexico. Market believed a full-scale trade war is less likely. Blue chips broadly fared well. US technology stocks outperformed blue chips, fuelling a five-day rise of Nasdaq Composite Index. HK technology stocks also outran, with Sunny Optical (2382.HK) soaring 7.5% to $143.80, being the strongest blue chip and handset equipment stocks were popular. While Tencent (700.HK) rose 0.9% to 447.00. In the consumption space, China Res Beer (291.HK) shot up 9.9% to 33.90 as word spread that the brewer is in talks on buying Chinese business of Heineken. Tsing Tao Brew (168.HK) grew 1.9%, last traded at 42.45. In earnings, MTR Corporation (66.HK) shares were in good shape, on 64% increase in annual profit and higher dividend – total ordinary dividend for the year was $1.12/share, mounted 4.1%, closed at $42.70. Oil prices were up early Monday after bouncing in the last session from recent falls.
